description: The frame of a board: columns side by side, as wide as the room allows and never narrower than one column's minimum, scrolling sideways when they no longer fit. It is one tab stop carrying a group role and a name, which is what a scrolling region needs to be reachable by keyboard at all. It draws no card and moves nothing: what a column holds is the consumer's, and reordering is theirs too.

label.description: Names the board to assistive technology: what the columns are columns OF. "Sprint 32 tasks by status", never "Board". Required and guarded at runtime after trimming, the shape ArenaScroller.label carries for the same reason, since a group announced as a group tells a reader that focus moved and nothing about where it landed.

content.description: The columns, one ArenaBoardColumn each. Required and guarded at runtime: a board with no columns is a tab stop over nothing, which is the dead stop a component with a group role must not ship.

minColumn.description: The narrowest a column may be before the board scrolls rather than squeezing. Columns share the room equally above it, so a board of four fills the width it is given and a board of twelve scrolls. It is a length rather than a step on the spacing scale, for the reason ArenaGrid.min is one: this is page geometry and the spacing scale models rhythm. The default is the same role a grid's cell reads, so a card is one width across a wall, a rail and a board.
